target_name: External Funding Load on Fixed Investment
rationale: This is essentially a mechanical product of two well-documented anomalies (asset/PP&E growth and net external financing, Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan), and scaling financing by capex rather than assets introduces a near-zero, sign-unstable denominator for asset-light firms that winsorization only partly tames, so the incremental content over the known composite is thin.

The multiplicative cash-decline INDICATOR zeroes out roughly half the cross-section, so the "short" leg is a genuine high-growth/high-issuance group while the "long" leg is an undifferentiated mass of ties at zero, making the portfolio spread an artifact of the dummy rather than a test of the stated warehoused-proceeds mechanism.

Because non-issuers are collapsed to zero below all issuers, the signal's cross-sectional variation is dominated by the net-share-issuance dummy (a known anomaly) rather than by capex acceleration, so the interaction as coded cannot isolate the hypothesized timing channel.

Economically coherent leveraged-empire-building interaction with a correctly signed monotone construction and no degenerate indicator, though aqc and Δgdwl are largely redundant and the mass of zero-acquisition firms will concentrate ties in the low leg.

Combining real operating-capacity expansion (inventory plus headcount) with short-maturity financing is a substantively different rollover-risk/fragility mechanism rather than a repackaging of asset growth, and the expression's direction matches the stated negative sign.

The signed funding-source contrast scaled by capex intensity is internally consistent with the positive expected sign, but Δcash and external issuance are mechanically positively correlated so the two legs largely duplicate one another, leaving the signal close to a capex-weighted restatement of the external financing anomaly and vulnerable to cash burn being read as "deployment."
